rationale: Peripheral axonal neuropathy presenting with clinically evident distal extremity drop (wrist drop and foot drop) is documented as an expansion of the classic NKX6-2 phenotype, first identified as a novel manifestation by Bereshneh et al. (2020) in two Iranian siblings. Subsequent clinical reviews, including Ganguly et al. (2023), specifically reference this presentation to those two siblings among the broader global cohorts of SPAX8 / hypomyelinating leukodystrophy cases. While generalized or mild peripheral neuropathy features are cited in broader differential discussions (Almatrafi et al., 2020; Sharma et al., 2025), overt distal extremity drop secondary to axonal neuropathy remains restricted to these isolated cases, firmly placing its frequency below 10% of reported NKX6-2 cases.

evidence.text: Bereshneh et al. (2020) documented two Iranian siblings carrying a homozygous c.501C>G, p.(Phe167Leu) missense mutation in NKX6-2 presenting with wrist and foot drop due to peripheral axonal neuropathy, explicitly identifying this as a novel clinical finding expanding the phenotype of SPAX8.

new_directions.question_text: What is the systematic prevalence of electrophysiologically proven subclinical peripheral axonal neuropathy across all published NKX6-2/SPAX8 cases?
new_directions.rationale: While clinically overt wrist and foot drop is rare, subclinical electrophysiological axonal involvement might be underdiagnosed if nerve conduction studies are not systematically performed in all cohorts.

new_directions.question_text: Is the p.(Phe167Leu) missense mutation uniquely associated with a severe peripheral axonal phenotype compared to homeobox domain truncating or other missense variants?
new_directions.rationale: Determining genotype-phenotype correlations could clarify whether axonal degeneration with distal drop is variant-specific rather than a generic end-stage feature of NKX6-2 loss.
